In mathematics, the '''Benjamin–Ono equation''' is a nonlinear partial [[integro-differential equation]] that 
describes one-dimensional [[internal wave]]s in deep water.
It was introduced by {{harvtxt|Benjamin|1967}} and {{harvtxt|Ono|1975}}.

The Benjamin–Ono equation is
:<math>u_t+uu_x+Hu_{xx}=0</math>
where ''H'' is the [[Hilbert transform]].

It possesses infinitely many conserved densities and symmetries; thus it is a completely integrable system.<ref>A two-parameter Miura transformation of the Benjamin-Ono equation, 
T.L. Bock, M.D. Kruskal, Physics Letters A, Volume 74, Issues 3–4, 12 November 1979, Pages 173-176.</ref>
